pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Many US beaches have lifeguards, but not every beach has one.
items.why: Lifeguards work at many popular beaches, often in the warm season. Look for the tower and the signs.

items.s: Sunscreen is only for hot summer days.
items.why: The sun can burn your skin on cloudy days too, so many people use sunscreen all year at the beach.

items.s: A red flag at a beach often means the water is dangerous.
items.why: Flag colors can change from place to place, so read the sign or ask the lifeguard.

pages.title: A warm day in Honolulu · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny day in Honolulu. Nora and her friend Serena walk to the sand. “**What a beautiful beach!**” Serena says. “**Yes! Is the water cold?**” Nora asks. “**No, it’s warm. Let’s swim!**”
“**Wait. I need sunscreen**,” Nora says. Her skin burns easily in the sun. “**Here, use mine**,” Serena says, and she gives Nora a bottle. Nora puts it on her face, her arms and her legs.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O “th” de “the” e “this” não existe em português. Brasileiros costumam falar “de” e “dis”, o que muda a palavra e soa estranho.
pages.how: Coloque a ponta da língua levemente entre os dentes da frente e deixe a voz vibrar enquanto o ar passa. A língua não deve ficar parada atrás dos dentes, como no d.
pages.tip: Segure o som de “thhh” por um segundo e depois solte a vogal: the, this.
